learningObjective: XOR writes sum-without-carry bits while shifted AND carries shared 1 bits into the next pass.

mechanismReview.pattern: Iterative binary addition: XOR for provisional sum and shifted AND for carry.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: The prompt forbids arithmetic addition and subtraction but permits bitwise operators on fixed-width signed integers.
mechanismReview.invariant: At every loop boundary, first plus second modulo 2^32 equals the original sum; each pass moves unresolved carries left until second becomes zero.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Retain only two masked 32-bit words: first holds sum bits not yet combined with carry, and second holds the shifted carry. The example displays four low bits because 7+5 does not touch higher bits.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: Named bit-place columns with stable sum-bit and carry-bit keys make the carry move left across passes and keep all binary arithmetic readable without color.
rejectedAlternatives: A decimal number line uses addition geometry and hides XOR/AND behavior.
A truth table explains one bit but does not show carry propagation across repeated word-level passes.
Showing only 7 -> 12 skips the simultaneous tuple update and the termination condition.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Separate a binary operation into local output and deferred carry state; the same decomposition underlies half/full adders, bit-mask arithmetic, and fixed-width overflow reasoning.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.

deckReview.notes: No source slide deck is part of the supplied coding guide. The visual was designed from this problem's source implementation and worked trace.
